TD Five Boro Bike Tour

Sunday, May 2, 2027

Sunday, May 2, 2027. The tour is always the first Sunday in May.

What is the TD Five Boro Bike Tour?

The TD Five Boro Bike Tour is a 40-mile, car-free ride through all five boroughs of New York City, held the first Sunday in May. It starts at Bowling Green in Lower Manhattan, crosses five bridges and finishes with a festival on Staten Island. Bike New York has run it since 1999, it draws 32,000 riders, and it began in 1977 as a bike-safety ride for high school students. The next edition is May 2, 2027.

Sign up for Five Boro Official site (bike.nyc)

Registration for the 2027 tour opened at noon on Tuesday, September 15, 2026 on Bike New York’s new haku platform. Standard, member, VIP and charity-team entries are sold separately; Bike New York members get a dedicated start wave. Proceeds fund Bike New York’s free bike-education programs.

How the TD Five Boro Bike Tour started

The ride started in February 1977, when Sal Cirami of American Youth Hostels met Eric Prager, who had been hired by the New York City Board of Education to build a bicycle-safety program. Prager’s plan included a day trip around the five boroughs. On June 10, 1977, about 250 people rode it: 50 high school students from five schools and 200 club cyclists. It started and ended at Flushing Meadows-Corona Park in Queens and covered 50 miles with one rest stop.

The next year Mayor Ed Koch backed a citywide ride, the distance was shortened, and ‘challenge’ became ‘tour’. TD Bank has sponsored it since 1992. In 1999 AYH decided the tour needed a dedicated organization and spun off Bike New York, which was established in 2000 and still runs it.

Today the tour brings 32,000 riders a year. Proceeds fund Bike New York’s free bike-skills classes, which have taught more than 100,000 kids and adults since 2007. The 2020 tour was cancelled because of COVID-19; it has run every year since.

What to expect on the day

The start is at Bowling Green at the bottom of Manhattan, reached by the Hudson River Greenway or Broadway. Riders are assigned to start waves; Bike New York members, VIP riders and charity riders each get a dedicated first wave. The route heads north through Central Park, into the Bronx, back down the FDR Drive, over the Queensboro Bridge into Queens, through Brooklyn and over the Verrazzano-Narrows Bridge into Staten Island.

Every street on the route is closed to cars. Rest areas along the way have snacks and entertainment, with extra water stops in between, free bike-repair labor, and SAG vehicles. Registration includes a rider packet with helmet cover, bib and bike plate, a special-edition finisher medal and entry to the Finish Festival on Staten Island.

It is a tour, not a race. With 32,000 riders the pace is slow at the start and the bridges bunch up. Bring a bike that works, a spare tube and patience. If you are flying in, Unlimited Biking is the official rental partner with pickup at 105 Broad Street, a few blocks from the start.

Weather in New York for the TD Five Boro Bike Tour

Early May in New York City averages a high of about 71°F and a low of about 56°F, and May has roughly 9.7 days with measurable rain, so plan for anything from cold drizzle to warm sun. The bridges are exposed and windy.

The town

Sleep, eat, fix the bike.

New York City is the largest city in the United States, with about 8.8 million people across five boroughs. The TD Five Boro Bike Tour starts at Bowling Green at the southern tip of Manhattan on the first Sunday in May and is the one day a year 40 miles of city streets and bridges are closed to cars. Riders base themselves in the Financial District, a short roll from the start.

Three airports serve the city. Newark (EWR) is about 13 miles from Lower Manhattan and JFK about 18; LaGuardia is closer to Queens. You do not want a car. Take a train or cab to a Financial District hotel and you can ride to the Bowling Green start in minutes. If you are shipping or renting a bike, Unlimited Biking, the tour’s official rental partner, has a downtown pickup at 105 Broad Street.

Group rides around New York

Free, recurring, open to anyone. Ride with locals the day before, or the week after.

  • NYC-ADV Saturday Adventure RidesNew York, NY · Saturday mornings, about every other week from May to fall, at 8:00 am. Season 11 so far: May 9, May 16, May 30, Jun 6, Aug 15, Aug 29 and Oct 10. Each ride is a new park.
  • Weekday Dawn Laps in Central Park (NYCC)New York, NY · Monday to Thursday before work. Several groups start between 5:40 and 6:50 am, sorted by lap time. A-level laps at 5:40 am on Tuesdays and Thursdays, B-level laps at 6:05 am on Tuesdays and Thursdays, Recovery Laps on Mondays at 6:25 am, a slower C group on Thursdays at 6:45 am. Each ride is two to four laps, 12 to 24 miles.
  • Women’s Wednesday (WTFNB only), Central ParkNew York, NY · Every Wednesday morning in Central Park, 6:50 to 8:00 am. Three laps at about 19 minutes a lap, 18 miles, B level, rotating paceline. Open to women, non-binary and trans riders only.
  • Five Borough Bicycle Club Day RidesNew York, NY · Most Saturdays and Sundays, plus some weekdays and holidays. Starts are usually between 9:00 and 10:30 am and change with the route

TD Five Boro Bike Tour FAQ

Is the route really closed to cars?

Yes. All 40 miles are car-free, including the FDR Drive, the Queensboro Bridge and the Verrazzano-Narrows Bridge.

How hard is it?

It is flat apart from bridge approaches. The main challenge is the crowd; 32,000 riders share the road, so expect stop-and-go sections.

Where do I start and finish?

Start at Bowling Green in Lower Manhattan. Finish at the Finish Festival on Staten Island, then ride to the Staten Island Ferry to return to Manhattan.

Can I rent a bike?

Yes. Unlimited Biking is the official rental partner. 2027 rentals start at $109 for a hybrid and $149 for a road bike, with downtown pickup at 105 Broad Street.

What does the entry fee support?

Bike New York’s free cycling-education programs across the city.

When does registration open?

For 2027 it opened at noon on September 15, 2026, on the haku platform linked from bike.nyc.
